target_customer: Consumer and business travelers searching for flights and hotels; revenue came from affiliate and booking fees paid by travel partners
problem: Flight search sites returned long, confusing lists that made it hard to compare price, duration and layovers.
business_model: travel search with per-booking referral fees (Orbitz paid about $3 per flight sold at launch)

founders.name: Adam Goldstein
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him founder and CEO, a former YC visiting partner and an O'Reilly author. Education and prior employers not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Steve Huffman
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder on the YC page; TechCrunch calls him a Reddit co-founder. Education not found in opened sources.

exit.reason: Concur retired the consumer site and Concur Hipmunk on 2020-01-23 as part of its travel and expense strategy

competitors.name: Kayak
competitors.traction_then: established leader; its CEO publicly dismissed Hipmunk

competitors.name: Orbitz
competitors.what: online travel agency, also Hipmunk's first data partner

technical_complexity.rationale: A graphical results view and agony sort on top of third party flight data. At launch all flights came via Orbitz; ITA QPX was licensed in November 2010. Standard engineering with a few hard UX parts.

defensibility.rationale: Same data as competitors and a UI that could be copied; the mascot and design polish were the main differentiators.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not kill it quickly; SAP Concur bought it in about 2016 (sources differ) and then retired it in January 2020.

market_need_then: Flight search was widely seen as painful; launch coverage in August 2010 praised the visual approach as a fix for an old, daunting problem.

branding.name_origin: After buying BouncePounce.com and Trot.me, Goldstein's girlfriend suggested building a brand around a cute mammal; Hipmunk was chosen (TechCrunch, 2010).
branding.domain_note: Founder bought several other domains before settling on the Hipmunk name; how hipmunk.com was acquired was not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: humorous, with Agony and Ecstasy sort names; Huffman's mantra was to be not horrible

branding.brand_signature: The scarf-wearing chipmunk and the Agony sort
branding.community_and_virality: Named in TIME 50 Coolest Websites and similar lists per the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Mascot and Agony sort were widely covered and praised by press; the YC profile lists multiple best-of awards.

outcome_analysis: Hipmunk won early attention with a distinctive visual flight search and a memorable mascot, raised about 40 million dollars across four rounds ending with a 2014 Series C, and was acquired by SAP Concur around 2016. Concur then shut the consumer product in January 2020, after the founders failed to buy it back, so the exit did not yield a lasting product.
notes: hipmunk.com returned HTTP 503 when fetched, so the site is treated as dead. Series B amount of 15 million with IVP leading comes from a search summary and fits the roughly 40 million total in TechCrunch; the round itself is dated by TechCrunch's link to a 2012-06-12 announcement. Acquisition year sources differ (Skift says 2016). Founder education and prior employers were not found.
